guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: Jangly acoustic-to-electric clean with swelling delay, then sustaining Marshall-style lead
tone.profile: Jangly acoustic-to-electric clean with swelling delay, then sustaining Marshall-style lead
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain starting with a light boost and compression for fingerpicked clarity. The core tone uses US Deluxe/Silver Twin settings to emulate the acoustic cleanliness, transitioning into UK 45 or UK 50 for the lead section, enhanced by Digital Delay and Plate reverb.

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - Stairway to Heaven - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise during quiet arpeggios.
Slightly boost signal level and add initial clarity for fingerpicking.
blocks.gap: A dedicated clean boost would be ideal, but Boost serves the function well.

blocks.purpose: Keep the initial tone clean and transparent for arpeggios.
Provide the bell-like, clean, and articulate tone for the acoustic/clean sections.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is a good proxy for early 60s Fender cleans, fitting the 'bell-like' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, articulate sound of a smaller American cabinet.
Keep the tone static and clean; V-Wah is included as a placeholder for potential texture.
blocks.gap: No specific modulation was requested, but WAH provides useful tonal shaping if needed later.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the clarity and 'jangly' quality of the arpeggios.
Provide the swelling delay effect crucial for the build-up and sustain.
Add warm, sustained ambience without sounding overly wet or wash-y.
blocks.gap: The Plate reverb is a good substitute for the requested 'small plate' sound.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR and amp simulation for British lead tone.

proposals.reason: The US cabinet is too bright for the required Marshall-style sustain and warmth in the solo section.
proposals.expectedGain: Warmer, thicker sound with better mid-range focus.

proposals.reason: The US Deluxe is too American for the required British Marshall lead tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Authentic British grit and sustain for the climax.
